title: 6.99 per WEEK!
body: Honestly, I don’t believe people should have to pay for full access to features that help them grow closer to God, such as scrolling videos that bring Bible stories to life. I was initially under the impression that this app was free, and I was genuinely excited about the opportunity to understand and interpret the Bible in a new and engaging way. Unfortunately, I was disappointed to discover that full access requires a paid subscription. I understand that developing an app takes time and resources, but I don’t believe access to tools that help people learn God’s Word should come at such a high cost. I’m certainly not willing to pay more for a Bible app than I am for Netflix which is not my cup of tea anyways. That money could be going toward tithes, supporting ministries, or helping those in need. **The Gospel is GOOD NEWS, and it should be shared freely.** We don’t ask unbelievers to pay us before we share the love of Jesus or speak life into them. We share the Gospel because we are called to do so. While I appreciate the creativity and effort behind this app, I truly believe the core features that help people engage with Scripture should be accessible to everyone, regardless of their financial situation. God’s Word is for everyone, not just those who can afford a subscription.

title: Misleading Paywall and Questionable Marketing Claims
body: I downloaded this app because it looked promising, but the experience was extremely disappointing. You spend time answering a series of introductory questions and getting everything set up, only to reach the end and discover that continuing requires an expensive weekly subscription. I would have appreciated seeing the cost clearly upfront rather than after going through the entire setup process. I was also surprised by the very high overall rating compared with the written reviews I found, many of which describe similar frustration with the paywall and subscription cost. The app also promotes claims such as having “30 million users” and being a “2026 Favorite App.” But it’s only been active in the App Store for 7 weeks. I would like to know the source for those claims. I could not find independent information explaining who designated it a 2026 favorite or substantiating the 30 million-user figure. The concept itself could be great, but transparency matters, especially for a faith-based app. Clearly disclose the subscription price before users spend time completing the introductory questions, and provide sources for major promotional claims.
